# `skyglow.webp`: whose work it is

`skyglow.webp` is a cut of the
[Light Pollution Atlas 2025](https://djlorenz.github.io/astronomy/lp/) by
**David J. Lorenz**.

The atlas is a model of how bright artificial light makes the sky overhead,
worked out from the VIIRS satellite's night-time lights (NOAA; the yearly
cloud-free composites of the Earth Observation Group, Colorado School of
Mines) by the method of the World Atlas of Artificial Night Sky Brightness
(Falchi and others, 2016).

**Changed:** reduced from his `world2025_low3.png` (a fortieth of a degree)
to a tenth of a degree, each cell the middle zone of its pixels; his five
darkest zones made one; and written as greys.

**The atlas states no license**, so there's no `LICENSE` file in this
folder. It's used here with credit to its author, in the app's About box
and in this file. `skyglow.webp` is his work, cut down: it isn't covered by
any license of the app's own.
